ety.text: From Middle English nest, nist, nyst, from Old English nest, from Proto-West Germanic *nest, from Proto-Germanic *nestą, from Proto-Indo-European *nisdós (“nest”), literally "where [the bird] sits down", a compound of *ni (“down”) (whence also English nether) + the zero-grade of the root *sed- (“to sit”) (whence also English sit).

From Middle English nesten, nisten, from Old English nistan, nistian, from Proto-West Germanic *nistijan (“to nest, build a nest”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian näästje (“to nest”), Dutch nesten (“to nest”), German Low German nüsten (“to nest”), German nisten (“to nest”).

senses.d: A structure built by a bird as a place to incubate eggs and rear young.
A place used by a mammal, fish, amphibian or insect, for depositing eggs and hatching young.
A snug, comfortable, or cosy residence or job situation.
A retreat, or place of habitual resort.
A hideout for bad people to frequent or haunt; a den.
ex: That nightclub is a nest of strange people!

senses.d: A home that a child or young adult shares with a parent or guardian.
ex: I am aspiring to leave the nest.

senses.d: A fixed number of cards in some bidding games awarded to the highest bidder allowing him to exchange any or all with cards in his hand.
ex: I was forced to change trumps when I found the ace, jack, and nine of diamonds in the nest.

senses.d: A fortified position for a weapon.
A structure consisting of nested structures, such as nested loops or nested subroutine calls.
ex: Our analysis to this point has assumed that in a loop nest, we are only parallelizing a single loop.

senses.d: A circular bed of pasta, rice, etc. to be topped or filled with other foods.
To build or settle into a nest.

ex: We loved the new house and were nesting there in two days!

senses.d: To successively neatly fit inside another.
ex: I bought a set of nesting mixing bowls for my mother.

senses.d: To place in, or as if in, a nest.
To place one thing neatly inside another, and both inside yet another (and so on).
ex: There would be much more room in the attic if you had nested all the empty boxes.

senses.d: To hunt for birds' nests or their contents (usually "go nesting").
ex: After the first heavy frost, when acorns were falling, I took a friend into partnership and went nesting.
